audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel 7 draft aligned to Kiriath-jearim custody, Israel's return, Mizpah, battle, Ebenezer, territorial recovery, peace, and Samuel's circuit; later source/witness audit required.
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Hebrew-first naming, restored/mystical separation, narrative ambiguity, institutional power, vulnerable persons, violence, and misuse risks.

verses.restored: Humans of Kiriath-jearim came and brought up ark of YHWH. They brought it to house of Abinadab on hill and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep ark of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the men of Kirjathjearim came, and fetched up the ark of the LORD, and brought it into the house of Abinadab in the hill, and sanctified Eleazar his son to keep the ark of the LORD.

modern.text: Then the men of Kiriath-jearim came for the ark of the LORD and took it into Abinadab’s house on the hill. And they consecrated his son Eleazar to guard the ark of the LORD.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ אַנְשֵׁ֣י קִרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֗ים וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ אֶת אֲר֣וֹן יְהוָ֔ה וַיָּבִ֣אוּ אֹת֔וֹ אֶל בֵּ֥ית אֲבִינָדָ֖ב בַּגִּבְעָ֑ה וְאֶת אֶלְעָזָ֤ר בְּנוֹ֙ קִדְּשׁ֔וּ לִשְׁמֹ֖ר אֶת אֲר֥וֹן יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: It happened from day ark rested at Kiriath-jearim that days multiplied and became twenty years. All house of Israel lamented/longed after YHWH.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, while the ark abode in Kirjathjearim, that the time was long; for it was twenty years: and all the house of Israel lamented after the LORD.

modern.text: And from that day a long time passed, twenty years in all, as the ark remained at Kiriath-jearim. And all the house of Israel mourned and sought after the LORD.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י מִיּ֞וֹם שֶׁ֤בֶת הָֽאָרוֹן֙ בְּקִרְיַ֣ת יְעָרִ֔ים וַיִּרְבּוּ֙ הַיָּמִ֔ים וַיִּֽהְי֖וּ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיִּנָּה֛וּ כָּל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אַחֲרֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Samuel said to all house of Israel, If with all your heart you are returning to YHWH, remove foreign gods and Ashtaroth from among you, establish your heart toward YHWH, and serve him alone; then he will rescue you from hand of Philistines.

familiar.text: And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto the LORD with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the LORD, and serve him only: and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.

modern.text: Then Samuel said to all the house of Israel, “If you are returning to the LORD with all your hearts, then rid yourselves of the foreign gods and Ashtoreths among you, prepare your hearts for the LORD, and serve Him only. And He will deliver you from the hand of the Philistines.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל אֶל כָּל בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵל֮ לֵאמֹר֒ אִם בְּכָל לְבַבְכֶ֗ם אַתֶּ֤ם שָׁבִים֙ אֶל יְהוָ֔ה הָסִ֜ירוּ אֶת אֱלֹהֵ֧י הַנֵּכָ֛ר מִתּוֹכְכֶ֖ם וְהָעַשְׁתָּר֑וֹת וְהָכִ֨ינוּ לְבַבְכֶ֤ם אֶל יְהוָה֙ וְעִבְדֻ֣הוּ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְיַצֵּ֥ל אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel removed Baals and Ashtaroth and served YHWH alone.

familiar.text: Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the LORD only.

modern.text: So the Israelites put away the Baals and Ashtoreths and served only the LORD.

original.text: וַיָּסִ֨ירוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֶת הַבְּעָלִ֖ים וְאֶת הָעַשְׁתָּרֹ֑ת וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת יְהוָ֖ה לְבַדּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Samuel said, Gather all Israel at Mizpah, and I will pray for you to YHWH.

familiar.text: And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the LORD.

modern.text: Then Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to the LORD on your behalf.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל קִבְצ֥וּ אֶת כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל הַמִּצְפָּ֑תָה וְאֶתְפַּלֵּ֥ל בַּעַדְכֶ֖ם אֶל יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: They gathered at Mizpah, drew water and poured it before YHWH, fasted on that day, and said there, We have sinned against YHWH. Samuel judged children of Israel at Mizpah.

familiar.text: And they gathered together to Mizpeh, and drew water, and poured it out before the LORD, and fasted on that day, and said there, We have sinned against the LORD. And Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpeh.

modern.text: When they had gathered at Mizpah, they drew water and poured it out before the LORD. On that day they fasted, and there they confessed, “We have sinned against the LORD.” And Samuel judged the Israelites at Mizpah.

original.text: וַיִּקָּבְצ֣וּ הַ֠מִּצְפָּתָה וַיִּֽשְׁאֲבוּ מַ֜יִם וַֽיִּשְׁפְּכ֣וּ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה וַיָּצ֨וּמוּ֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וַיֹּ֣אמְרוּ שָׁ֔ם חָטָ֖אנוּ לַיהוָ֑ה וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֧ט שְׁמוּאֵ֛ל אֶת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בַּמִּצְפָּֽה

verses.restored: Philistines heard that children of Israel had gathered at Mizpah, and lords of Philistines went up against Israel. Children of Israel heard and were afraid before Philistines.

familiar.text: And when the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together to Mizpeh, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. And when the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.

modern.text: When the Philistines heard that the Israelites had gathered at Mizpah, their rulers marched up toward Israel. And when the Israelites learned of this, they feared the Philistines

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ פְלִשְׁתִּ֗ים כִּֽי הִתְקַבְּצ֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ הַמִּצְפָּ֔תָה וַיַּעֲל֥וּ סַרְנֵֽי פְלִשְׁתִּ֖ים אֶל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּשְׁמְעוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֥י פְלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: Children of Israel said to Samuel, Do not be silent from crying out for us to YHWH our God, that he may deliver us from hand of Philistines.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel said to Samuel, Cease not to cry unto the LORD our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.

modern.text: and said to Samuel, “Do not stop crying out to the LORD our God for us, that He may save us from the hand of the Philistines.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֤וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֶל שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל אַל תַּחֲרֵ֣שׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ מִזְּעֹ֖ק אֶל יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֑ינוּ וְיֹשִׁעֵ֖נוּ מִיַּ֥ד פְּלִשְׁתִּֽים

verses.restored: Samuel took one sucking lamb and offered it whole as an ascending offering to YHWH. Samuel cried out to YHWH for Israel, and YHWH answered him.

familiar.text: And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the LORD: and Samuel cried unto the LORD for Israel; and the LORD heard him.

modern.text: Then Samuel took a suckling lamb and offered it as a whole burnt offering to the LORD. He cried out to the LORD on behalf of Israel, and the LORD answered him.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֣ח שְׁמוּאֵ֗ל טְלֵ֤ה חָלָב֙ אֶחָ֔ד ויעלה עוֹלָ֛ה כָּלִ֖יל לַֽיהוָ֑ה וַיִּזְעַ֨ק שְׁמוּאֵ֤ל אֶל יְהוָה֙ בְּעַ֣ד יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַֽיַּעֲנֵ֖הוּ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: As Samuel was offering ascending offering, Philistines drew near for battle against Israel. YHWH thundered with a great voice on that day against Philistines, confused them, and they were struck before Israel.

familiar.text: And as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel: but the LORD thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them; and they were smitten before Israel.

modern.text: As the Philistines drew near to fight against Israel, Samuel was sacrificing the burnt offering. But that day the LORD thundered loudly against the Philistines and threw them into such confusion that they fled before Israel.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י שְׁמוּאֵל֙ מַעֲלֶ֣ה הָעוֹלָ֔ה וּפְלִשְׁתִּ֣ים נִגְּשׁ֔וּ לַמִּלְחָמָ֖ה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּרְעֵ֣ם יְהוָ֣ה בְּקוֹל גָּ֠דוֹל בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא עַל פְּלִשְׁתִּים֙ וַיְהֻמֵּ֔ם וַיִּנָּגְפ֖וּ לִפְנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: Humans of Israel went out from Mizpah, pursued Philistines, and struck them as far as below Beth-car.

familiar.text: And the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh, and pursued the Philistines, and smote them, until they came under Bethcar.

modern.text: Then the men of Israel charged out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, striking them down all the way to an area below Beth-car.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨צְא֜וּ אַנְשֵׁ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מִן הַמִּצְפָּ֔ה וַֽיִּרְדְּפ֖וּ אֶת פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיַּכּ֕וּם עַד מִתַּ֖חַת לְבֵ֥ית כָּֽר

verses.restored: Samuel took one stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen. He called its name Ebenezer, saying, Thus far YHWH has helped us.

familiar.text: Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Ebenezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.

modern.text: Afterward, Samuel took a stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, saying, “Thus far the LORD has helped us.”

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח שְׁמוּאֵ֜ל אֶ֣בֶן אַחַ֗ת וַיָּ֤שֶׂם בֵּֽין הַמִּצְפָּה֙ וּבֵ֣ין הַשֵּׁ֔ן וַיִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמָ֖הּ אֶ֣בֶן הָעָ֑זֶר וַיֹּאמַ֕ר עַד הֵ֖נָּה עֲזָרָ֥נוּ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Philistines were subdued and did not continue to enter border of Israel. Hand of YHWH was against Philistines all days of Samuel.

familiar.text: So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

modern.text: So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped invading the territory of Israel. And the hand of the LORD was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.

original.text: וַיִּכָּֽנְעוּ֙ הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְלֹא יָסְפ֣וּ ע֔וֹד לָב֖וֹא בִּגְב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַתְּהִ֤י יַד יְהוָה֙ בַּפְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י שְׁמוּאֵֽל

verses.restored: Cities that Philistines had taken from Israel returned to Israel, from Ekron as far as Gath, and Israel rescued their territory from hand of Philistines. There was peace between Israel and Amorites.

familiar.text: And the cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even unto Gath; and the coasts thereof did Israel deliver out of the hands of the Philistines. And there was peace between Israel and the Amorites.

modern.text: The cities from Ekron to Gath, which the Philistines had taken, were restored to Israel, who also delivered the surrounding territory from the hand of the Philistines. And there was peace between the Israelites and the Amorites.

original.text: וַתָּשֹׁ֣בְנָה הֶעָרִ֡ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לָֽקְחוּ פְלִשְׁתִּים֩ מֵאֵ֨ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֤ל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ מֵעֶקְר֣וֹן וְעַד גַּ֔ת וְאֶ֨ת גְּבוּלָ֔ן הִצִּ֥יל יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מִיַּ֣ד פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֣י שָׁל֔וֹם בֵּ֥ין יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וּבֵ֥ין הָאֱמֹרִֽי

verses.restored: Samuel judged Israel all days of his life.

familiar.text: And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

modern.text: So Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁפֹּ֤ט שְׁמוּאֵל֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו

verses.restored: He went from year to year and made circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah, and judged Israel in all these places.

familiar.text: And he went from year to year in circuit to Bethel, and Gilgal, and Mizpeh, and judged Israel in all those places.

modern.text: Every year he would go on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging Israel in all these places.

original.text: וְהָלַ֗ךְ מִדֵּ֤י שָׁנָה֙ בְּשָׁנָ֔ה וְסָבַב֙ בֵּֽית אֵ֔ל וְהַגִּלְגָּ֖ל וְהַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְשָׁפַט֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֥ת כָּל הַמְּקוֹמ֖וֹת הָאֵֽלֶּה

verses.restored: His return was to Ramah, for there was his house, and there he judged Israel. He built there an altar to YHWH.

familiar.text: And his return was to Ramah; for there was his house; and there he judged Israel; and there he built an altar unto the LORD.

modern.text: Then he would return to Ramah because his home was there, and there he judged Israel and built an altar to the LORD.

original.text: וּתְשֻׁבָת֤וֹ הָרָמָ֨תָה֙ כִּֽי שָׁ֣ם בֵּית֔וֹ וְשָׁ֖ם שָׁפָ֣ט אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיִּֽבֶן שָׁ֥ם מִזְבֵּ֖חַ לַֽיהוָֽה

translation_notes: Kiriath-jearim receives and houses the ark for twenty years. Sacred custody is responsibility, not ownership of Divine presence.
Israel's lamenting or longing after YHWH conveys communal desire and grief, not ethnic purity.

Samuel's command to remove Baals and Ashtaroth belongs to Israel's covenant exclusivity. It may not authorize religious persecution, destruction of others' sacred property, coercive conversion, or antisemitic/supersessionist claims.
Public confession is communal practice, not permission to compel individual disclosure or stage humiliation.
Fasting and pouring water are ritual actions whose exact meanings require audit; they are not mandatory techniques for earning deliverance.
Philistine military action is reported without making all Philistines timeless enemies.
Samuel's intercession does not establish clergy as gatekeepers who can sell access to God.
The sucking lamb sacrifice reflects an ancient animal-offering system and should not be reenacted or sentimentalized.
Thunder and battle confusion are narrated as Divine aid, but the ensuing pursuit remains violence and cannot become a universal holy-war model.
Ebenezer means stone of help. Memorials should remember dependence and loss, not erase casualties or become territorial triumphalism.
Territorial recovery and peace with Amorites are both reported; peace is not lesser than military success.
Samuel's circuit shows distributed access to judgment, though the narrative does not audit whose voices were excluded.
Samuel builds an altar at Ramah; this should not override later centralization traditions or authorize private religious domination.
safety_note: Do not use covenant exclusivity to persecute other religions or destroy sacred objects. Do not glorify war, animal sacrifice, coerced confession, or territorial domination. Ebenezer remembers help, not ethnic superiority. Philistines and Amorites remain human communities, and peace is a central good.
